title: CMOSP18 FD-SOI Technology Based MCU Achieving High Performance of 1.2GHz Using High Speed, Optimized Leakage & High Density Tightly Coupled Memory (TCM)
problem: Microcontroller units (MCUs) require both high performance (>1GHz) and low-leakage operation. Tightly coupled memories (TCM) are critical for processor performance but consume significant power and area. Optimizing TCM for both speed and leakage is challenging without degrading performance.
method: Two TCM variants in CMOSP18 FD-SOI technology: (1) performance-optimized instances for TCM placed closer to core (standard timing); (2) leakage-optimized instances for far TCM placement (reduced VDD, optimized gates). Both use high-density bitcells to reduce area and RC delay.

title: HELM: Characterizing Unified Memory Accesses to Improve GPU Performance under Memory Oversubscription
problem: Unified Memory default migration policies severely degrade performance under memory oversubscription; existing solutions fail to generalize across applications
method: HELM metrics derived from UM driver telemetry to characterize access patterns; metrics guide selection of optimal UM migration policies

title: Security of Approximate Neural Networks against Power Side-channel Attacks
problem: Security implications of approximate computing in Artificial Neural Networks; understanding vulnerability to power side-channel attacks as approximate computing techniques (overclocking, voltage scaling, bitwise approximation) are deployed for energy reduction.
method: Evaluates power side-channel vulnerability of approximate ANN processing elements under three approximation scenarios: (1) overclocking, (2) voltage scaling, (3) circuit-level bitwise approximation. Performs weight extraction correlation power analysis (CPA) attacks; measures Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) degradation and Measurement-to-Disclosure (MTD) metric; analyzes trade-off via Security-Power-Delay (SPD) metric.

title: 37.6 A 22nm 60.81TFLOPS/W Diffusion Accelerator with Bandwidth-Aware Memory Partition and BL-Segmented Compute-in-Memory for Efficient Multi-Task Content Generation
problem: Existing CIM accelerators struggle with diffusion model efficiency due to: large operational intensity variation across layers creating dynamic bandwidth needs, 10x larger data storage than GANs/VAEs, system-level CIM efficiency degradation despite high macro efficiency, 59% CIM power consumed on data access, and 31% of operations spent on computationally-intensive multi-view/temporal attention.
method: 22nm CIM accelerator with bandwidth-aware memory partitioning to match dynamic layer requirements, BL-segmented compute-in-memory macros optimizing data reuse, and specialized operators for multi-view/temporal attention consistency in 3D/video tasks.

title: Stability-preserving Lossy Compression for Large-scale Partial Differential Equations
problem: Checkpoint/restart (C/R) strategies are vital for fault tolerance in large-scale PDE simulations, but lossy compression risks instability due to loss of physical invariants (e.g., energy), leading to oscillations and divergence.
method: Stability-preserving lossy compression explicitly controlling kinetic and potential energy perturbations to ensure stable PDE restarts. Extensive evaluation across diverse PDE configurations on Frontier supercomputer.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper Caracal: A GPU-Resident Sparse LU Solver with Lightweight Fine-Grained Scheduling
problem: Reproducibility of HPC systems research requires independent verification of claims and results. The Caracal paper claims significant speedups over existing sparse solvers.
method: Artifact evaluation following SC25 Artifact Description and Evaluation (AE) guidelines. Independent testing of Caracal implementation, reproduction of reported results, verification of claimed speedups.

title: Tropical: Enhancing SLO Attainment in Disaggregated LLM Serving via SLO-Aware Multiplexing
problem: Disaggregated LLM serving isolates prefill and decode on separate workers to optimize one phase but creates high queuing delays; non-disaggregated serving reduces queuing but causes compute interference between phases, violating latency SLOs (TTFT, TPOT).
method: Tropical introduces SLO-aware multiplexing that dynamically balances prefill and decode execution on hybrid workers to leverage benefits of both disaggregated (low interference) and non-disaggregated (low queuing) architectures. Uses adaptive scheduling to minimize queuing delays while controlling interference, enabling simultaneous TTFT and TPOT SLO compliance.

title: BitMoD: Bit-serial Mixture-of-Datatype LLM Acceleration
problem: LLM deployment is constrained by large weight memory footprints; existing low-precision quantization schemes either sacrifice too much accuracy or lack hardware support for multiple heterogeneous data types simultaneously. Current accelerators cannot efficiently process mixed numerical formats (e.g., INT4, FP4, NF4) within a single design.
method: BitMoD is an algorithm-hardware co-design that introduces fine-grained per-group (128-weight) data-type adaptation, selecting from a set of carefully designed numerical types to minimize quantization error per group. On the hardware side, a bit-serial processing element natively handles multiple precisions by decomposing weights into bit-planes; a unified representation maps all data types to a common internal format, and a dedicated bit-serial dequantization unit rescales per-group partial sums with minimal overhead.

title: LowDiff: Efficient Frequent Checkpointing via Low-Cost Differential for High-Performance Distributed Training Systems
problem: Frequent checkpointing for fast failure recovery in distributed deep learning training generates numerous checkpoints, incurring substantial storage costs and degrading training performance.
method: LowDiff reuses compressed gradients (already computed in distributed training) as differential checkpoints to reduce storage costs. Includes batched gradient write optimization and dynamic tuning of checkpoint frequency and batching size.

title: HPIM-NoC: A Priori-Knowledge-Based Optimization Framework for Heterogeneous PIM-Based NoCs
problem: Existing NoC simulators and architecture search frameworks are designed for homogeneous architectures and lack support for simulating and optimizing heterogeneous Processing-in-Memory (PIM) configurations with varied core capabilities.
method: HPIM-NoC implements a joint simulation and search framework supporting heterogeneous PIM cores with accurate latency modeling via NoC transmission delays and pipelines. It uses a three-stage heterogeneous search process based on priori knowledge with a customized simulated annealing algorithm, accelerated by precomputing core PPA metrics and reducing NoC simulation frequency, plus a customized layout algorithm.

title: 12.2 p-Circuits: Neither Digital Nor Analog
problem: Traditional analog and digital circuits present inherent trade-offs in power, area, and performance; a new computing paradigm is needed that combines benefits of both without requiring ADC/DAC conversions.
method: p-circuits introduce a probabilistic computing model where circuit inputs and outputs maintain digital-like interfaces (no ADC/DAC), but the output is a random binary variable whose probability P(B=1) is governed by an analog function A(inputs) that continuously varies between 0 and 1. This enables stochastic computation where probability encodes information.

title: Extending the C++ Execution Control Library to Support Dynamic Parallel Runtime Systems
problem: C++26 execution control library (senders and receivers) provides interface for asynchronous work coordination on heterogeneous backends, but lacks integration with dynamic runtime systems that create work at runtime and expose massive oversubscription.
method: Implement sender-based interface for Qthreads user-level threading library, demonstrating that C++26 execution control patterns (senders/receivers) extend to dynamic runtime systems where work is discovered and created dynamically.

title: Accelerating LLM Serving for Multi-turn Dialogues with Efficient Resource Management
problem: Current LLM serving frameworks recompute attention keys and values for all prior turns on each new query in a multi-turn dialogue, incurring substantial redundant compute overhead. Additionally, the long accumulated prompt lengths from multi-turn context cause head-of-line blocking under FCFS scheduling, underutilizing GPU resources.
method: The paper introduces efficient resource management for multi-turn LLM serving by preserving KV-cache state across turns to eliminate recomputation of prior-turn attention keys and values. A new scheduling policy replaces FCFS with a length-aware or priority-based scheduler that avoids head-of-line blocking by reordering or preempting long-prompt requests. KV-cache memory is managed dynamically to balance cache retention across concurrent multi-turn sessions, trading off memory capacity against recompute cost.

title: 19.9 An 11-to-16.4GHz, 3.4GHz/µs-Slope, 5.32GHz-Chirp-Bandwidth, 0.043%-RMS-Frequency-Error FMCW Digital PLL with Posterior-Segment DPD Featuring 5-Chirp-Cycle Convergence Time
problem: FMCW radars for autonomous driving and IoT require wide-bandwidth chirps with high linearity and fast convergence to multiple frequency bands; multi-vehicle interference and multi-mode operation demand rapid frequency-hopping and DPD convergence within single chirp bursts.
method: 11-to-16.4GHz digital PLL with posterior-segment digital predistortion (DPD) that converges in 5 chirp cycles, generating chirps with 3.4GHz/µs slope and 5.32GHz bandwidth, achieving 0.043% RMS frequency error despite nonlinearity.

title: eIM: GPU-Accelerated Efficient Influence Maximization in Large-Scale Social Networks
problem: Influence maximization (IM) in large networks is NP-hard. State-of-the-art GPU IMM (Influence Maximization via Martingales) algorithm incurs significant memory overhead from storing random reverse reachable (RRR) sets, limiting scalability.
method: eIM: GPU-accelerated IMM algorithm with optimized memory efficiency. Reduces RRR set storage requirements while maintaining algorithm correctness. Achieves similar accuracy to baselines with improved memory utilization.

title: BurstEngine: An efficient distributed framework for training transformers On extremely Long sequences of over 1M tokens
problem: Training LLMs on long sequences (>1M tokens) exhibits low Model FLOPs Utilization with Tensor Parallelism and Context Parallelism, especially as sequence lengths and GPU counts increase.
method: BurstEngine framework introducing: (1) BurstAttention with topology-aware ring communication and fine-grained communication-computation overlap, (2) sequence-level selective checkpointing, (3) language modeling head-loss fusion, (4) workload balance optimization for attention masking.
